name: LHCb collaboration
source: LHCb collaboration document 'Template for writing LHCb papers' (Documentation_instructions_CERN_LHCb.pdf), Section 6 'Figures' and the Layout guidelines.
rules: Figures must be easy to read at the size they will be printed, with suitable line widths.
Every axis must have a label with suitable units, chosen so the tick numbers don't run together (e.g. GeV/c^2 rather than MeV/c^2 when the range covers several GeV).

Figures with LHCb data must say "LHCb" on them, or "LHCb preliminary" for preliminary results, "LHCb simulation" for simulation-only figures, and no label for figures that don't depend on LHCb-specific software.
Figures with LHCb data must show the integrated luminosity (e.g. "9 fb^-1" on a line below "LHCb"); cross-section or heavy-ion papers may show the centre-of-mass energy instead.
Label the y axis "Entries" or "Candidates" if no background subtraction was applied, otherwise "Yield" or "Decays", and give the bin width when showing yield per bin, e.g. "Entries / (5 MeV/c^2)".
Fit curves must not hide the data points, which are best drawn on top of the fit curves.
Colour is allowed, but differently coloured lines and areas must still be told apart in black and white, for example with different dash styles or hatching.
Never use the rainbow palette for two-dimensional plots; use printer-friendly, colour-blind-safe palettes such as those from colorbrewer2.org.
Use different hatching styles to separate filled areas, and avoid ROOT hatch styles 3001-3025 (3345 and 3354 are good falling and rising hatches).
Axis labels and legends should use the same font as the main text, upright rather than slanted, or consistently upright sans-serif, but never a mix of styles.
Particle symbols in figures should use the same roman or italic style as the text.
Minus signs in figure labels must be proper minus signs, not hyphens.
Avoid spurious background shading and boxes around text, including legend frames.
Figures with more than one part must label the parts (a), (b), etc., or refer to them clearly by position, and describe each in the caption.

Captions go below the figure in a slightly smaller typeface, are short and correctly punctuated, don't start with an article, describe the data before the fit components, and contain no numbered equations.
Pull plots are normally not shown in papers unless they highlight regions where the fit fails.
Figure files go in the figs/ directory as PDF for pdflatex (EPS for plain LaTeX).
